lessons.title: Introduction and Why It Matters
lessons.body: Finishing is the difference between a metal piece that looks like scrap and one that sells for top price. In African markets, a well-finished metal chair or table can fetch 40-60% more than an unfinished one. Finishing protects against rust, which is the number one killer of metal furniture in humid coastal cities like Mombasa, Lagos, or Durban. It also adds colour, texture, and style that match local tastesâfrom bright powder-coated colours popular in Nairobi to antique patinas favoured in Marrakech. Without finishing, even the strongest welded frame will corrode within months, especially during rainy seasons. You have three main options: paint (cheap, easy, but less durable), powder coating (tough, professional, needs electricity and a oven), and patina (chemical treatment that gives an aged, artistic look). Each has its place. For a beginner, paint is the best starting point because you can do it in your workshop with minimal equipment. Powder coating requires sending pieces to a specialist, but itâs worth it for high-end clients. Patina is for artistic pieces and restoration work. This module will teach you all three, step by step, using tools and materials available in most African cities. By the end, youâll be able to finish a metal stool or table that looks professional and lasts for years. Remember: finishing is 30% of the total work time but 70% of the customerâs first impression. Donât rush it.

lessons.title: Tools and Materials
lessons.body: To do a professional finish, you need the right tools. For painting: an angle grinder with a wire cup brush (for removing rust and old paint), sandpaper (80, 120, 220 grit), clean rags, a spray gun or aerosol cans, and a compressor if using a gun. For powder coating, youâll need a powder coating gun (if doing it yourself) or a local powder coater, an oven that reaches 200Â°C, and a sandblasting setup or chemical stripper. For patina: chemical solutions like liver of sulfur, copper sulfate, or ferric chloride, plus a torch for heat patina, and wax or lacquer for sealing. Essential safety gear: nitrile gloves, respirator mask (not just a dust mask), safety goggles, and a fire extinguisher. In Africa, you can source most of these from hardware stores in big cities or from online suppliers like Jumia or local industrial markets. For paint, use automotive-grade acrylic enamel or epoxy paintâthey cost more but last 3-5 times longer than cheap enamel. A 1-litre can of quality paint covers about 8-10 square metres. For powder coating, polyester powders are best for outdoor furniture. For patina, you can make your own copper sulfate solution by dissolving 50g of copper sulfate in 1 litre of water. Always buy from reputable suppliers; fake chemicals wonât give consistent results. Budget: a basic paint finishing kit (grinder, sandpaper, spray gun, compressor) costs around $300-500. Powder coating setup is $800-1500. Patina chemicals are cheap ($20-50). Start with paint, then add powder coating when you have steady orders.

lessons.title: Step by Step Method
lessons.body: Step 1: Preparation. Remove all rust, mill scale, and old paint using an angle grinder with a wire cup brush. Then sand with 80-grit, then 120-grit, then 220-grit for a smooth surface. Wipe down with a clean rag and a degreaser (acetone or lacquer thinner). Any oil or dust will cause the finish to peel. Step 2: Priming. For paint, apply a metal primer (zinc phosphate or epoxy) within 30 minutes of cleaning. Spray a thin coat, let it flash off for 10-15 minutes, then apply a second coat. For powder coating, the metal is first sandblasted or chemically cleaned, then the powder is sprayed electrostatically and baked at 200Â°C for 10-15 minutes. For patina, you skip primer and apply chemicals directly to clean metal. Step 3: Application. For paint, spray two to three thin coats, waiting 15-20 minutes between coats. Keep the gun 20-25 cm from the surface and move in steady passes. For powder coating, the piece is hung and grounded, then powder is sprayed until a uniform layer forms, then baked. For patina, brush or spray the chemical solution, let it react for 5-20 minutes, then rinse with water and dry. Step 4: Sealing. For paint, no sealing needed if using quality paint. For powder coating, the baking process is the seal. For patina, apply a clear lacquer or wax to stop the reaction and protect the finish. Step 5: Curing. Let paint cure for 24-48 hours before use. Powder coating is ready immediately after cooling. Patina should cure for 24 hours before handling. Always test on a small scrap piece first.

lessons.title: Common Mistakes and Fixes
lessons.body: Mistake 1: Not cleaning the metal properly. Dust, oil, or rust will make paint or powder flake off. Fix: always degrease with acetone and sand to bare metal. Mistake 2: Applying too thick a coat. Thick paint runs, sags, and takes forever to dry. Fix: apply multiple thin coats instead of one thick one. Mistake 3: Painting in humid or dusty conditions. Humidity causes blushing (white haze) and dust sticks to wet paint. Fix: paint in a well-ventilated but dust-free area, ideally indoors with a fan. If humidity is above 70%, wait for a dry day. Mistake 4: Using the wrong thinner. Cheap thinner can react with paint and cause orange peel. Fix: use the thinner recommended by the paint manufacturer. Mistake 5: Not grounding the piece for powder coating. Without proper grounding, powder wonât stick. Fix: ensure the hook and rack are clean and conductive. Mistake 6: Overheating powder coating. If the oven is too hot or the piece bakes too long, the powder turns yellow or brittle. Fix: use an oven thermometer and stick to 200Â°C for 10-15 minutes. Mistake 7: Patina turning out too dark or uneven. Fix: dilute the chemical, apply in thin layers, and build up slowly. Mistake 8: Skipping the sealing step on patina. Without sealer, the patina will continue to react and may rub off on clothes. Fix: always apply a clear coat or wax. Mistake 9: Not letting paint cure fully. Using the furniture too soon causes scratches. Fix: wait 48 hours. Mistake 10: Using a dirty spray gun. This causes spitting and uneven finish. Fix: clean your gun immediately after every use with the appropriate solvent.

lessons.title: Safety and Best Practice
lessons.body: Finishing involves chemicals and processes that can harm you if youâre careless. Always wear nitrile gloves when handling paint, thinners, and patina chemicals. Latex gloves are not enoughâthey dissolve. Wear a respirator mask with organic vapour cartridges when spraying paint or powder. A dust mask is useless against fumes. Work in a well-ventilated area: open doors and windows, use a fan to blow fumes away from you, and never work in a closed room. Keep a fire extinguisher nearby because paint thinners and solvents are highly flammable. Store chemicals in original labelled containers, away from heat and children. For powder coating, the oven must be in a separate, fireproof area. Never use a home oven for powder coatingâresidues are toxic. For patina, some chemicals like liver of sulfur smell like rotten eggs; work outdoors or with strong ventilation. Best practices: mix only what you need, never return used chemicals to the original container, and dispose of waste properlyânever pour down the drain. Keep a first aid kit with eye wash and burn cream. If you get chemicals on your skin, wash immediately with soap and water. If in eyes, rinse for 15 minutes and seek medical help. Also, protect your work area with drop cloths or cardboard. And always test your finish on a scrap piece before applying to the final product. Finally, maintain your tools: clean spray guns, change respirator cartridges regularly, and inspect hoses for leaks. Safety is not optionalâitâs part of professionalism.

lessons.title: Practical Exercise
lessons.body: For this exercise, you will finish a small metal stool or side table using paint. You will need: one bare metal stool (welded and cleaned), 80/120/220 grit sandpaper, angle grinder with wire brush, acetone, clean rags, metal primer, acrylic enamel paint (colour of your choice), spray gun or aerosol cans, respirator, gloves, and a dust-free area. Step 1: Grind all welds and rust with the wire brush, then sand with 80, 120, and 220 grit. Wipe with acetone. Step 2: Spray a thin coat of primer. Wait 15 minutes, then spray a second coat. Let dry for 1 hour. Step 3: Spray the first colour coat. Keep the gun 20 cm away, use steady passes. Wait 20 minutes. Spray second coat. Wait 20 minutes. Spray third coat if needed for full coverage. Step 4: Let cure for 48 hours. Step 5: Inspect for runs, dust, or missed spots. If found, sand lightly with 400 grit and touch up. Step 6: Take a photo and compare with a professionally finished piece. Note what you could improve. For extra practice, try a patina on a small piece of scrap metal: clean it, apply copper sulfate solution, let it react, rinse, dry, and seal with wax. Record the time and results. This exercise should take 3-4 hours over two days. Once you can consistently produce a smooth, even finish, you are ready to charge clients for finishing services. Remember: the quality of your finish determines your reputation.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Finishing Metal Furniture for African Markets

This practical reference is the working companion to the six lessons in Finishing: Paint, Powder, Patina. It is written for the small and growing metal furniture workshop â the kind found in Kariobangi, Nnewi, Kumasi Suame Magazine, or along Mombasa Road â where a welder, two apprentices, and a sprayer turn steel into beds, gates, school desks, and cafÃ© chairs. Finishing is where your margin lives. A well-finished piece of furniture sells for 30â60% more than the same piece left in raw primer, and it survives the rainy season, the coastal salt air, and the harmattan dust that destroy poorly finished work.

Use this page as a bench-side reference. Print it, laminate it, and hang it near the spray booth. The tables, diagram, and checklist are designed to be used, not just read.

Table 1: Finishing Method Selection by Product, Market, and Climate

Product / Market Recommended Finish Typical DFT Cure / Process Time Indicative Material Cost (USD/mÂ²) Why This Choice
Interior school desks, office chairs (Kenya, Ghana, Nigeria) Powder coat, polyester 60â80 Âµm 200Â°C / 10â15 min oven 1.80â3.20 Durable, low VOC, fast line throughput; premium institutional look
Outdoor gates, burglar bars (coastal: Mombasa, Dar, Lagos) Zinc-rich epoxy primer + polyurethane topcoat 160â220 Âµm total 7-day full cure 3.50â6.00 Salt-air corrosion resistance; ISO 12944 C4/C5 environment
Outdoor gates (inland: Nairobi, Kumasi, Abuja) Etch primer + alkyd enamel 100â140 Âµm total 24â48 h touch-dry 1.20â2.40 Good UV and rain resistance at lower cost; widely available
Decorative / heritage patina (artisan market, export) Chemical patina + clear lacquer 25â40 Âµm clear 24 h 2.00â5.50 Sells as handcrafted; high margin in tourist and export channels
Budget beds, school lockers (informal market) Red oxide primer + gloss enamel 80â120 Âµm total 12â24 h 0.80â1.60 Lowest cost, available everywhere, acceptable for dry indoor use

Costs are indicative 2024â2025 workshop-gate estimates for East and West Africa; verify with your local supplier. DFT ranges and environment categories follow ISO 12944-2 and 12944-5.

Table 2: Common Defects, Root Causes, and Fixes

Defect Root Cause Fix / Prevention Cost Impact
Paint peeling / flaking within 3 months Mill scale, rust, or oil left on steel; no primer Grind to SSPC-SP 3 or better; degrease with solvent; apply primer within 4 hours Full rework â 100% of finish cost plus labour
Runs and sags on vertical surfaces Over-thinning, too-heavy coat, wrong spray distance Follow TDS thinning ratio; 20â25 cm spray distance; apply thin wet coats Sand and recoat â 20â30% extra material
Powder coat "orange peel" or pinholes Contaminated compressed air, moisture in line, low oven temp Install air dryer and oil filter; verify oven temp with a datalogger; check gun kV Strip and recoat â 100% of powder cost
Patina looks blotchy or uneven Uneven application of patina solution; inconsistent surface prep Work in sections; use consistent spray distance and dwell time; test on offcuts first Cosmetic rework â 30â50% extra labour
Topcoat blushing (white haze) in humid weather Moisture condensing in film during cure; high humidity Add retarder thinner; avoid spraying when RH > 85%; spray early morning Sand and recoat â 20â40% extra material
Colour mismatch between batches Different pigment lots; inconsistent film thickness Buy one batch for the whole order; mix all cans together; use a DFT gauge Customer rejection risk â can lose the order

Defect categories and corrective actions align with American Coatings Association and SSPC guidance on coating failures, adapted for small African workshops.

â  RED SAFETY WARNING â Isocyanate and Solvent Exposure

Two-pack polyurethane and epoxy hardeners contain isocyanates. Isocyanate exposure can cause occupational asthma, which is permanent and can be fatal. Solvent-based paints and thinners can cause chronic nerve damage and are highly flammable.

Mandatory controls in every African workshop:

  • Wear a supplied-air respirator or an approved organic vapour / particulate cartridge mask â a dust mask is not enough.
  • Spray only in a well-ventilated booth or open-sided structure; never in a closed room.
  • Keep no ignition sources within 10 m; store thinners in a locked, grounded metal cabinet.
  • Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection; wash skin immediately after contact.
  • Keep a dry powder or COâ fire extinguisher within 5 m of the spray area.
  • Train every worker on the safety data sheet (SDS) before first use â this is a legal requirement in Kenya (DOSHS), Nigeria (NOSH), and Ghana (GSA).

If a worker develops wheezing, chest tightness, or shortness of breath after spraying, stop work and seek medical attention immediately. Report the exposure.

Quick Reference Checklist â Bench-Side Card

  1. Inspect and prep steel: Remove mill scale, rust, weld spatter, and oil. Grind to bare metal on all visible surfaces. Wipe with solvent and let flash off.
  2. Apply pretreatment: Zinc or iron phosphate conversion coat on all surfaces, including edges and inside tubes where possible. Rinse and dry fully.
  3. Prime within 4 hours: Apply epoxy or zinc-rich primer at the specified DFT. Check with a gauge. Do not leave bare steel overnight in humid conditions.
  4. Mix and thin correctly: Follow the technical data sheet (TDS) exactly. Use the correct thinner, at the correct ratio, at the correct temperature.
  5. Control the environment: Spray when temperature is 15â30Â°C and relative humidity is below 85%. Avoid direct sun and strong wind.
  6. Apply build and topcoats: Thin wet coats, 20â25 cm spray distance, 50% overlap. Allow flash-off between coats.
  7. Inspect before cure: Check for runs, sags, pinholes, and dry spray. Fix defects before the film hardens.
  8. Cure and protect: Respect full cure time before handling, packing, or delivery. Stack with foam or paper between finished parts.

Further Reading â Free Official Resources

  • SSPC â The Society for Protective Coatings: Free technical guides on surface preparation (SP 1, SP 3, SP 6) and coating application.
  • ISO 12944-5:2019 â Protective paint systems: International standard for corrosion protection of steel structures, including environment classification for coastal and inland Africa.
  • OSHA â Occupational Safety and Health Administration: Free guidance on spray booth ventilation, respirator selection, and isocyanate safety.
  • American Coatings Association: Free articles on coating defects, troubleshooting, and application best practice.
  • UNIDO â United Nations Industrial Development Organization: Free technical reports on metal fabrication and finishing for small and medium enterprises in Africa.

Business note: Every hour spent on correct surface preparation and controlled application returns three to five hours in avoided rework, customer complaints, and lost repeat orders. In the African metal furniture market, your reputation is your order book. Finish like your next contract depends on it â because it does.

quiz.q: What is the main benefit of finishing metal furniture?
options: B) It protects against rust and increases value
C) It makes it easier to weld
D) It reduces the need for cleaning
quiz.explanation: Finishing protects against rust and can increase selling price by 40-60%.

quiz.q: Which finishing method is best for a beginner with minimal equipment?
quiz.explanation: Paint requires only basic tools and can be done in a small workshop.

quiz.q: What is the correct order of sandpaper grits for preparing metal?
quiz.explanation: Start with coarse 80 to remove rust, then 120, then 220 for smoothness.

quiz.q: Why must you degrease metal before painting?
options: B) To remove oil and dust so paint sticks
quiz.explanation: Oil and dust prevent paint adhesion, causing peeling.

quiz.q: What temperature is used for baking powder coating?
quiz.explanation: Powder coating typically bakes at 200Â°C for 10-15 minutes.

quiz.q: Which chemical is commonly used for a copper patina?
quiz.explanation: All three can be used for different patina effects.

quiz.q: What safety gear is essential when spraying paint?
options: B) Respirator with organic vapour cartridges
quiz.explanation: A dust mask does not protect against paint fumes; a proper respirator is needed.

quiz.q: What happens if you apply paint too thickly?
quiz.explanation: Thick coats cause runs, sags, and long drying times.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid painting in high humidity?
options: B) Causes blushing and poor adhesion
quiz.explanation: High humidity can cause a white haze (blushing) and prevent proper curing.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a primer on metal?
options: B) To improve paint adhesion and prevent rust
quiz.explanation: Primer provides a base for paint and adds corrosion protection.

quiz.q: How long should paint cure before using the furniture?
quiz.explanation: Paint needs 24-48 hours to fully cure and harden.

quiz.q: What is a common mistake when powder coating?
quiz.explanation: Overheating and poor grounding both ruin the powder coating finish.

quiz.q: How can you fix a patina that is too dark?
options: B) Dilute the chemical and apply thinner layers
quiz.explanation: Diluting and applying in thin layers allows you to control the darkness.

quiz.q: Why must you seal a patina finish?
options: B) To stop the chemical reaction and protect it
quiz.explanation: Sealer stops the patina from continuing to react and rubbing off.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a recommended practice for finishing?
options: A) Cleaning your spray gun after use
C) Using a home oven for powder coating
quiz.explanation: Home ovens can leave toxic residues and are not safe for powder coating.

quiz.q: What is the approximate coverage of 1 litre of quality paint?
quiz.explanation: A litre of paint typically covers 8-10 square metres in one coat.

quiz.q: What is the best way to remove rust before finishing?
options: B) Angle grinder with wire cup brush
quiz.explanation: A wire cup brush on an angle grinder quickly removes rust and mill scale.

quiz.q: Why is it important to work in a well-ventilated area?
options: B) To avoid breathing toxic fumes
C) To keep the metal cool
quiz.explanation: Paint and chemical fumes are harmful; ventilation keeps you safe.

quiz.q: What is the recommended distance for spray gun from the surface?
quiz.explanation: 20-25 cm ensures even coverage without runs or dry spray.

quiz.q: Which type of paint is best for outdoor metal furniture?
quiz.explanation: Acrylic enamel and epoxy are durable and weather-resistant.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get paint thinner on your skin?
options: B) Wash with soap and water
quiz.explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water prevents irritation.

quiz.q: What is a sign of a properly cured powder coating?
options: B) It is hard and smooth
quiz.explanation: Properly baked powder coating is hard, smooth, and durable.

quiz.q: Why is it important to clean metal with acetone before painting?
options: B) It removes all oils and contaminants
quiz.explanation: Acetone removes oils that would prevent paint adhesion.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of powder coating over paint?
options: B) More durable and professional finish
C) Easier to do at home
quiz.explanation: Powder coating is tougher and gives a more uniform, high-quality finish.

quiz.q: How long should you wait between coats of paint?
quiz.explanation: 15-20 minutes allows the paint to flash off before the next coat.

quiz.q: What is a common cause of orange peel texture in paint?
options: B) Wrong thinner or too cold
quiz.explanation: Incorrect thinner or cold conditions can cause orange peel.

quiz.q: What should you do before applying patina to a metal piece?
options: B) Clean it to bare metal
quiz.explanation: Patina chemicals need direct contact with clean metal to react.

quiz.q: Which of these is a best practice for storing chemicals?
options: C) In original labelled containers away from heat
quiz.explanation: Proper storage prevents accidents and maintains chemical potency.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a tack cloth or clean rag before painting?
quiz.explanation: Dust particles cause rough finishes; a tack cloth removes them.

quiz.q: In the practical exercise, how long should the finished painted stool cure before use?
quiz.explanation: 48 hours allows the paint to fully harden and cure.
